findings.title: House, ascent, and readable book
findings.claim: The house of gold, climb into the sky, and book brought down for the challengers to read form a route from visible status through privileged access to control of the proof's final format.
findings.mechanism: The focus pairs bayt with zukhuruf, then tarqa with al-sama, then tunazzila with kitaban naqra'uhu. The earlier spring, garden, and sky demands in 17:90-92 make this another step in a staged proof protocol; 17:78 and 17:82 already place Quranic recitation and descent in the scene. Meeting that public, already active medium with the challengers' own reading condition changes the final book into a specified mode of inspection.
findings.reader_payoff: The sequence becomes legible as a progression from owned display to access above to a document whose reading they prescribe.
findings.containment: The literal alternatives remain a decorated or gold house and an ascent, followed by a demanded descended book. The route is an interpretive organization of those terms; it does not claim that any demand is fulfilled or that the book is already the same object as the recited Quran.

epistemic.reason: The focus and pericope contacts are explicit, while the status-to-access-to-inspection route is a synthesis of trusted channel support rather than a lexical gloss.

findings.title: Human messenger and human recipients
findings.claim: The focus's human-messenger identity is named as the objection in 17:94, then 17:95 answers with a habitat counterfactual: settled walkers on earth receive an angelic messenger only in a world whose inhabitants are angels.
findings.mechanism: Before the following context, humanity can sound like a limitation the speaker simply confesses. After it, bashar rasulan meets the stated barrier to belief and the counterfactual matching the recipients' habitat and kind to the messenger's. The packet supplies that objection and match; the inference is that human embodiment is a recipient-suited medium.
findings.reader_payoff: The human messenger predicate reads as a qualification for communication with human recipients, as well as an answer to the demand for a different kind of envoy.
findings.containment: The medium-recipient principle is an inference. The following ayah may be read more narrowly as a rebuttal to an angelic-messenger demand; this finding does not generalize a rule to every messenger or audience.

epistemic.reason: The following Arabic context and HFT coordinates align with the focus words; the broader communication-fit principle is explicitly an inference.

findings.title: The Lord authorizes and witnesses
findings.claim: The focus's glorification of the Lord and the speaker's human-messenger identity meet a surrounding frame of Lord-given authority, truth's arrival, and God's final sufficiency as witness; together they can read as a boundary between the envoy's task and the Lord's authority.
findings.mechanism: Before the context, subhana rabbi can sound like a pious refusal to perform. After 17:80 asks the Lord for supporting authority, 17:81 lets truth arrive and falsehood vanish, and 17:96 names God as sufficient, informed, seeing witness, the focus's rabbi and rasul contact a role allocation: the messenger speaks and carries while authorization and final witness belong to the Lord.
findings.reader_payoff: The response becomes a jurisdictional correction as well as a refusal of the challengers' display protocol.
findings.containment: The packet's live alternative is that 17:80-81 and 17:96 are independent assurances rather than one role-boundary mechanism. The finding does not make the messenger's plain human identity disappear or claim more authority detail than these supplied verses provide.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context coordinates align, but the jurisdictional allocation is explicitly an inference and the source leaves the surrounding assurances separable.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus answers with subhana rabbi and the identity of a human messenger.
branch_activations.activation: Lord-given support meets the focus's attribution of transcendence and the speaker's bounded messenger role.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Proof and authorization are located with the Lord while the speaker remains a messenger.
branch_activations.boundary: The registry is unresolved for this HFT branch; the authority role stays attributed.

findings.title: A limited oral-healing echo
findings.claim: The focus words tarqa and ruqiyyika retain their ascent sense, while 17:82's Quran-as-healing and recitation supply an exploratory root-branch echo of protective spoken efficacy beside the demanded book the challengers will read themselves.
findings.mechanism: Before context, the demanded ascent is purely spatial. After 17:82, healing and Quranic recitation meet the focus's r-q-y carrier and the separate naqra'uhu reading act; the contact adds distrust of mediated oral efficacy as a possible coloring, without changing the grammatical ascent.
findings.reader_payoff: The sequence can carry both a physical ascent and a limited echo about spoken healing and control of reading.
findings.containment: The focus form is ascent, not an incantation. The ruqya branch is a root-level echo and never the lexical translation of tarqa or ruqiyyika; the manuscript demand may also simply distinguish a physical document from recitation.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch has a supplied lexicon record and the 17:82 healing/recitation coordinates match, but the branch-distant echo is explicitly surprising and its HFT source is unbound.

findings.title: Gold and withdrawable revelation
findings.claim: An attributed gold-branch echo joins the focus's zukhuruf house and written book to 17:86's removal of what was revealed: possessable display meets revelation that can depart.
findings.mechanism: Before context, the gold house is a separate luxury request. After 17:86, its word-index-3 root ذ ه ب occurrence, whose supplied contextual reading is going away, meets the focus gold branch at zukhuruf; the revealed content at word 5 and the focus book provide the second contact. The result is a material hinge between demanded property and withdrawable revelation, not a new lexical translation of the context verb.
findings.reader_payoff: The demand for a gold house and book can be seen beside a context that locates revealed content outside the challengers' custody.
findings.containment: The actual 17:86 occurrence remains a removal/going-away verb. Its gold branch is unresolved and survives only as the HFT-attributed hinge with focus zukhuruf; this does not claim that 17:86 means gold or that the focus book is the revealed content being removed.

epistemic.reason: The root coordinate and focus return match the packet, but the gold branch under the contextual verb has no independent registry gloss and the support explicitly marks this as a surprising hinge.

friction_notes: All seven HFT records are legacy_unbound. Their supplied source ayah/word-index/root coordinates match the focus QAC or context root-occurrence evidence, but the HFT roles remain attributed and many context branches have no independent registry gloss or facet.

The six explicitly added Fātiḥa ayat were reviewed only after the pericope phase. Their Lord reference and path request add no specific local contact that materially changes 17:93, so no external-overlay finding survives.
